title: LRU and LFU caches
idea: A cache keeps a bounded set of key-value pairs. When full, it evicts the least recently used (LRU) or least frequently used (LFU) key.

analogy.text: Your desk holds two open books. LRU shelves the one you touched longest ago. LFU shelves the one you have opened least often.
analogy.breaks: A desk never has to find a book in constant time.

points: A `HashMap` gives O(1) lookup; a second structure remembers who to evict.
LRU keeps a doubly linked list: hits move to the front; the tail leaves.
LFU groups keys by use count and evicts the oldest in the lowest group.
In real code, put both behind one `Cache<K, V>` interface to swap policies.

steps.caption: Both caches have capacity 2. `put("a")` adds `a`: front of the LRU list, count 1 in LFU.
`put("b")` puts `b` in front for LRU. In LFU it ties with `a` at count 1.
`get("a")` is a hit. LRU moves `a` to the front; LFU raises its count to 2.
A second `get("a")`. LRU order does not change; LFU count rises to 3.
`get("b")` makes `b` the newest for LRU, and gives it count 2 in LFU.
`put("c")` finds both caches full. LRU evicts its tail: `a`, touched longest ago.
LFU evicts the lowest count: `b`, used twice against three for `a`.
Same calls, different victims. LRU bets on recent use; LFU bets on long-run popularity.

code.title: LRU from scratch
code.caption: A `HashMap` plus a doubly linked list with sentinels. Every operation is O(1).

walk.text: Each node carries its key, so eviction can also remove it from the map.
`get` returns `null` on a miss; a hit moves the node to the front.
A new key on a full cache evicts `tail.prev`, the least recent node.
New or updated, the node ends at the front with its new value.
Sentinels mean no null checks: unlink is two pointer writes, push is four.
`main` replays the access pattern from the animation.

code.title: LFU with count groups
code.caption: Same calls as the LRU demo. A different key is evicted.

walk.text: Values, counts, and keys grouped by count. `minCount` points at the rarest group.
`bump` moves a key up one group and advances `minCount` if its group emptied.
The victim is the first key in the `minCount` group: rarest, then oldest.
A new key starts at count 1, so `minCount` resets to 1.

pitfalls: Never scan the whole map to pick a victim; that makes every `put` O(n).
Guard shared caches with a lock; these classes are not thread-safe.
Treat `put` on an existing key as a use: update recency or count too.

quiz.q: What is the first line `LfuCacheDemo` prints?
quiz.why: `a` was used three times and `b` twice. LFU evicts the lowest count, so `b` leaves; LRU would evict `a`.

takeaway: A map for lookup plus an order structure for eviction: that is every cache.

starters: Can I build an LRU cache with LinkedHashMap instead?
How would I make this cache thread-safe without one big lock?
When is LFU a worse choice than LRU?
